answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. A quartz of per-task receipts records who did what, and the ocean of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, released only after three unrelated confirmations, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the vertex of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
